cases.source: def run(x: bool) -> int; case x; when false; 7; when true; 9; else; missing; end; end
cases.difference: Rust follows the reachable match or loop path and does not check the skipped undefined-variable expression. The Rust witness completes without evaluating it; Go reports it.

cases.source: def run(x: int | string) -> int; case x; when 7; x+"bad"; else; 9; end; end
cases.difference: Rust narrows the matched input to an integer and rejects its addition to a string. Go emits no checker warning; the Rust witness reaches the corresponding runtime error.

cases.difference: Equality with an integer can match an equal float; Rust preserves that float possibility at the int return boundary. Go emits no checker warning; the Rust witness reaches the corresponding runtime error.
